purpose: Build the AuralMaximizerPro cross-platform C++20 / JUCE audio plugin (Standalone, VST3, CLAP, LV2) as a sequence of small, real-time-safe, independently verifiable tasks. Each DSP and GUI module is authored header-first then implementation, wired into the APVTS processor and split-screen editor, and gated by an incremental Standalone build. Because Abracapocus ships no C++ adapter (only Python/TypeScript/Go/C) and the C adapter covers .c/.h but not .cpp and defaults verification to make, this plan does not rely on adapter auto-detection: every task uses exact per-file allowed_write_paths (never globs) and every phase specifies its verification explicitly as a CMake/Ninja build plus cppcheck and clang-format, not make. Real-time-thread safety (no heap allocation, no locks, ScopedNoDenormals, smoothed parameters, lock-free SPSC audio-to-UI transfer) is a hard constraint on every audio-path task.
async_strategy: Phases run strictly sequentially; each phase is a synchronous verification boundary. Within a phase, tasks with disjoint allowed_write_paths run in the same wave. Wave 1 creates class headers (.h) and other standalone files; Wave 2 creates the matching implementations (.cpp) and depends on its own header; the final wave writes the phase verification artifact under docs/verification/ and depends on all implementation tasks. Files that appear in more than one phase (Source/PluginProcessor.cpp in phases a, e, h; Source/PluginEditor.* in phases a, h; each DSP/GUI file stubbed in phase a then implemented later) are never co-written inside a single phase, so phase ordering alone serializes them. VERIFICATION STACK (applies to every phase_verification.json): the C adapter's default make command MUST be overridden. Per-task focused verification compiles the AuralMaximizerPro_Standalone target only via 'cmake -B cmake-build-debug -G Ninja' then 'cmake --build cmake-build-debug --target AuralMaximizerPro_Standalone'; phase lint/format uses 'cppcheck --enable=all Source/' and 'clang-format --dry-run --Werror' on the phase's changed files. The full four-format build (VST3, CLAP, LV2) is gated once in phase i, never after every task. Backend routing is cost-first: codex_cli (CLI default model) for the hardest DSP/FFT/APVTS math; antigravity_cli (agy default = Gemini) for medium work; OpenCode+OpenRouter GLM 5.2 for lighter code; OpenCode+OpenRouter DeepSeek V4 Pro (or Gemma for trivial) for stubs-adjacent and documentation. Nothing is routed to Claude; claude_code_cli is reserved as a manual plan-patch fallback for tasks the cheaper backends fail.
operator_questions: No C++ adapter exists in create_default_registry(); the C adapter detects CMakeLists.txt at 0.95 and covers .h but NOT .cpp, and its suggest_verification returns make. This plan compensates with exact per-file allowed_write_paths and explicit CMake/cppcheck/clang-format verification in every phase. Proceed with those in-plan overrides (sufficient to build), or first approve adding a real C++ adapter to Abracapocus (abracapocus/languages/cpp_adapter.py + registry registration + quality_doctrine.md) as a separate prerequisite change? (Flagged, not bundled, per the no-architecture-change rule.)

CMakeLists.txt is classified as config by the C adapter and is write-protected by the write policy; task a.1 lists it explicitly in allowed_write_paths. Confirm the write policy permits config-file writes when the exact path is declared, so phase a can author the build file.

CLAP is not emitted by stock JUCE 7 or 8; it requires the free-audio clap-juce-extensions module and a clap_juce_extensions_plugin() call in CMakeLists.txt. Approve adding that submodule/dependency, or drop CLAP from FORMATS for the initial build?
Confirm JUCE is vendored as a git submodule at ./JUCE so add_subdirectory(JUCE) resolves, and pin JUCE 7 vs 8 (LV2 is stable in JUCE 7.0.6+; JUCE 8 changes some juce::dsp and font APIs).

The OpenRouter model IDs openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.2 and openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro are real but are not in Abracapocus's empirically-validated list (only gemma-4-31b-it is). Validate each backend+model pair with 'opencode run --dir "$PWD" -m <model> "Reply only with SUCCESS"' before phase execution, or approve as-is.

phases.goal: Establish the build system and a compiling empty plugin shell. Create the root CMakeLists.txt (JUCE subdirectory, C++20, juce_add_plugin with COMPANY_NAME nSpace / CODE Axpr, FORMATS Standalone VST3 CLAP LV2, link juce_audio_utils/juce_audio_processors/juce_dsp/juce_gui_basics/juce_gui_extra, juce_generate_juce_header) and a minimal empty stub (.h/.cpp) for every class in target_sources so the tree configures with Ninja and builds the Standalone target green. Materialize into one file-scoped task per file, not a single broad task. Each stub must compile against JUCE but contain no real DSP or layout yet: the processor stub returns a juce::GenericAudioProcessorEditor (it must NOT include PluginEditor.h, to keep the processor and editor tasks on disjoint write paths); the editor stub is a bare juce::AudioProcessorEditor.

Final wave: a.10 writes docs/verification/phase_a_build_skeleton.md and depends on a.1, a.2, a.3, a.4, a.5, a.6, a.7, a.8, a.9. No two tasks in this phase write the same file.
phases.risk_notes: Verification: phase_verification.json must run 'cmake -B cmake-build-debug -G Ninja' then 'cmake --build cmake-build-debug --target AuralMaximizerPro_Standalone' plus 'clang-format --dry-run --Werror' on the created files; do NOT use the C adapter default make. CMakeLists.txt is a config/protected file authored only by a.1 via exact allowed_write_paths. target_sources references every stub path, so the tree configures but does not build until all stubs exist; keep a.10 in the final wave. The processor stub must use juce::GenericAudioProcessorEditor and must NOT include PluginEditor.h, or a.2 and a.3 collide. CLAP/LV2 wrapper generation may fail configure if the JUCE version or clap-juce-extensions is missing (see operator_questions); the phase gate targets Standalone only.

phases.goal: Implement Module A, the Sonic Maximizer (phase alignment and dynamic low contour). Header first, then implementation. Pre-allocate all state in prepareToPlay(sampleRate, samplesPerBlock) with zero heap allocation, locks, or juce::String work in process(): 3-band split (low < MAX_LOW_FREQ, mid, high > MAX_HIGH_FREQ) using juce::dsp::IIR::Filter cascades; cascaded 1st/2nd-order allpass filters giving frequency-dependent group delay (4x APF on the low band, 2x on mid, 0x on high) with coefficient a = (tan(pi*fc/fs) - 1)/(tan(pi*fc/fs) + 1); an envelope follower e[n] = (1-alpha)*|x_low[n]| + alpha*e[n-1] with alpha = exp(-1/(0.05*sampleRate)); and dynamic boost G_low[n] = 1 + LoContour*(e[n]/(1+e[n])). Split into header-declares-state and cpp-implements-math tasks.
phases.async_notes: Wave 1: b.1 writes Source/DSP/SonicMaximizer.h only (band-filter members, APF cascade arrays, envelope state, prepare/process signatures). Wave 2: b.2 writes Source/DSP/SonicMaximizer.cpp only and depends on b.1. Final wave: b.3 writes docs/verification/phase_b_sonic_maximizer.md and depends on b.2. No same-file overlap.
phases.risk_notes: Verification: cmake/Ninja Standalone build plus 'cppcheck --enable=all Source/DSP' and clang-format on the two files; not make. Real-time safety is the primary risk: any new/delete/resize or juce::String in process() must be rejected. APF coefficient and envelope constants must be recomputed only in prepareToPlay or on parameter change, never per-sample from raw parameter reads. Header and cpp are serialized by dependency.

phases.goal: Implement Module B, the Aural Exciter (sidechain saturation and harmonics). Header first, then implementation, real-time safe with all buffers and the oversampler pre-allocated in prepareToPlay. Requirements: a 2nd-order high-pass sidechain via juce::dsp::StateVariableFilter with cutoff EXC_TUNE in [800 Hz, 10 kHz]; three selectable wave-shapers on the high-passed signal (Cubic Soft Clipping with the piecewise 2/3 and 4/3 thresholds; Asymmetric Tube y = tanh(G*x + delta) + gamma*(G*x)^2 with delta approx 0.15 for even harmonics and gamma from EXC_HARMONICS; Tape y = (2/pi)*arctan(G*x)); the non-linear stage wrapped in juce::dsp::Oversampling<float> with selectable 2x/4x polyphase FIR; and a post-saturation high-shelf Air EQ above 10 kHz driven by EXC_AIR_GAIN. Split header vs implementation.
phases.async_notes: Wave 1: c.1 writes Source/DSP/AuralExciter.h only (SVF member, Oversampling member, wave-shaper mode, air-EQ high-shelf, prepare/process signatures). Wave 2: c.2 writes Source/DSP/AuralExciter.cpp only and depends on c.1. Final wave: c.3 writes docs/verification/phase_c_aural_exciter.md and depends on c.2. No same-file overlap.
phases.risk_notes: Verification: cmake/Ninja Standalone build plus cppcheck --enable=all on Source/DSP and clang-format on the two files; not make. Oversampling must be constructed and its latency queried in prepareToPlay, never in process(). Drive gain G, delta bias, and gamma must be smoothed off the per-sample raw parameter path to avoid zipper noise. The exciter must not introduce locks or allocations.

phases.goal: Implement Module C, the Routing / Matrix engine. Header first, then implementation. Pre-allocate all scratch buffers in prepareToPlay (no allocation in process()). Support three routing modes selected by ROUTING_MODE: Serial Maximizer -> Exciter, Serial Exciter -> Maximizer, and Parallel Matrix Blend y = (1-K)*S_M(x) + K*S_E(x) where K is PARALLEL_BLEND smoothed with juce::SmoothedValue<float> to avoid clicks on mode/blend changes. The engine owns the two modules' invocation order and the crossfade summing; it must not itself allocate or lock.
phases.async_notes: Wave 1: d.1 writes Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h only (mode enum, pre-allocated scratch buffers, SmoothedValue crossfader, prepare/process signatures). Wave 2: d.2 writes Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp only and depends on d.1. Final wave: d.3 writes docs/verification/phase_d_routing_engine.md and depends on d.2. No same-file overlap.
phases.risk_notes: Verification: cmake/Ninja Standalone build plus cppcheck and clang-format on the two files; not make. Scratch buffers for the parallel path must be sized to samplesPerBlock and channel count in prepareToPlay. Switching routing mode at runtime must not reallocate; the crossfader smoothing prevents summing-bus clicks. Depends conceptually on phases b and c existing (guaranteed by phase order).

phases.goal: Integrate the DSP into PluginProcessor and stand up the APVTS. Header first, then implementation (both re-write the phase-a stub, single-owner within this phase). The header declares the APVTS member, owned SonicMaximizer / AuralExciter / RoutingEngine instances, a lock-free SPSC ring buffer (juce::AbstractFifo + std::array<float,N>) for audio-to-UI spectrum transfer, latency state, and prepare/process declarations. The implementation builds createParameterLayout() with all 19 parameters exactly as specified (MAX_ENABLE, MAX_PROCESS, MAX_CONTOUR, MAX_LOW_FREQ, MAX_HIGH_FREQ, MAX_PHASE_MODE, EXC_ENABLE, EXC_TUNE, EXC_DRIVE, EXC_MIX, EXC_MODE, EXC_HARMONICS, EXC_AIR_GAIN, ROUTING_MODE, PARALLEL_BLEND, MASTER_IN_GAIN, MASTER_OUT_GAIN, MASTER_MIX, OVERSAMPLING) with their ranges/defaults/skews; pre-allocates everything in prepareToPlay; runs processBlock with juce::ScopedNoDenormals at the top, input gain -> RoutingEngine -> output gain/dry-wet, atomic/SmoothedValue parameter reads, and pushes spectrum frames into the FIFO; and reports latency via setLatencySamples() based on the oversampling factor. Keep createEditor returning the generic editor for now (the real editor is wired in a later phase).
phases.async_notes: Wave 1: e.1 writes Source/PluginProcessor.h only (APVTS, DSP members, SPSC FIFO, latency, signatures). Wave 2: e.2 writes Source/PluginProcessor.cpp only and depends on e.1. Final wave: e.3 writes docs/verification/phase_e_processor_apvts.md and depends on e.2. No same-file overlap; PluginProcessor.{h,cpp} were last written in phase a and are re-authored here as single owner.
phases.risk_notes: Verification: cmake/Ninja Standalone build plus cppcheck and clang-format on the two files; not make. ScopedNoDenormals must be the first statement in processBlock. All 19 parameter IDs/ranges/defaults must match the specification table exactly or downstream editor attachments break. Latency reporting must track the selected oversampling factor. Do NOT wire the real PluginEditor here (later fan-in phase) to keep createEditor stable.

phases.goal: Implement the two independent GUI display components: the FFT SpectrumVisualizer and the L/R MeterComponent. These live in separate files, so their headers run in parallel and their implementations run in parallel. SpectrumVisualizer uses juce::dsp::FFT with a lock-free juce::AbstractFifo ring buffer consumed on a juce::Timer at 30 Hz on the message thread; it must never touch the audio thread directly and must only read frames the processor pushed into the SPSC FIFO. MeterComponent renders real-time L/R peak/RMS LED bars, also updated on a capped Timer. Neither component allocates in any audio-thread callback.

Final wave: g.5 writes docs/verification/phase_g_gui_components.md and depends on g.2 and g.4. The two components never share a write path.

phases.goal: Assemble the PluginEditor and attach every control to the APVTS. Header first, then implementation, then a single-line re-wire of the processor's createEditor. The editor header declares the fixed 920x540 window, the CustomLookAndFeel instance, all knobs/combos/toggles, the embedded SpectrumVisualizer and MeterComponent, and the APVTS attachment members. The implementation lays out the split-screen wireframe (left: Sonic Maximizer in cyan, right: Aural Exciter in amber with the FFT display, bottom: master routing/matrix/I-O in green), assigns accent colours, and binds every parameter with juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState::SliderAttachment / ComboBoxAttachment / ButtonAttachment to the exact 19 parameter IDs. A separate task then updates PluginProcessor.cpp so createEditor() returns the real PluginEditor instead of the generic editor.
